parts.title: SPIRAL REVIEW (5 min)
content: 1. GRAMMAR SPIRAL: Add the correct PEEL label (P/E/E/L) to each sentence: a) 'One major cause of ocean pollution is plastic waste.' b) 'According to Greenpeace, 8 million tonnes of plastic enter the ocean yearly.' c) 'This shows the scale of the problem is enormous.' d) 'In addition to this, the effects on marine animals are equally devastating.'

2. VOCABULARY: Complete using PEEL vocabulary: 'A [factor/aspect] in climate change is rising temperatures. This [demonstrates] that urgent action is [required]. A [comprehensive/logical] solution must address both causes and effects.'

3. MATH SPIRAL: Your report has 5 body paragraphs. Each has 5 sentences = 25 sentences. Plus introduction (6) + conclusion (5) = total report = ___ sentences. If the average sentence is 12 words, how many words total?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Each body paragraph in your Passion Project report should follow the PEEL structure. PEEL is an acronym that helps you build a logical, well-supported paragraph.
content: 📖 Each body paragraph in your Passion Project report should follow the PEEL structure. PEEL is an acronym that helps you build a logical, well-supported paragraph.
P — POINT: The first sentence states the main idea of the paragraph. It should directly answer one of your sub-questions. A strong point sentence is clear and specific.
E — EVIDENCE: The second and third sentences present evidence from your research. Use direct quotes or paraphrases with citations.
E — EXPLANATION: The fourth sentence explains what the evidence means and how it supports your point. This is your analysis — your thinking.
L — LINK: The final sentence connects this paragraph to the next one, or restates how the point supports your thesis.
A complete PEEL paragraph is usually 4-6 sentences long. With 5 sub-questions and 5 body paragraphs, your report will be comprehensive and well-organized.
